description: Executable cache conformance plans. CACHE-SEMANTICS.md is the contract they measure; every case id names an exchange in the wire corpus.

checklist.requirement: A repeated identical cached operation costs one wire request.
Concurrent identical cached operations cost one wire request, and every caller is answered.
Every operation outside the cached set reaches the wire on every call, including the scheme resource reads.
Argument order does not create a second entry, a member passed as unset does not either, and an explicit null does.
Two operations sharing a route and body keep separate entries.
A rejected request is not cached; the next call retries.
A malformed 200 is not cached: the response check runs inside the cached call, and the next call retries.
One caller canceling settles only that caller.
The wire request is canceled only when its last caller has gone.
On a pinned binding an entry survives arbitrarily long, past any TTL.
On an unpinned binding an entry expires, and no later than one hour.
Access decisions reach the wire on every call by default.
Once the opt-in is on, access decisions are cached like any other entry.
The opt-in is refused on an unpinned binding.
The never operations reach the wire on every call, opt-in or not.
A composition change clears the cache.
The runtime's denial-shaped 404 clears the cache; a resource 404 does not.

responseGate.description: Hold a matched request in flight at the transport until a release step answers it.

clock.description: Move the clock the response cache reads, so lifetimes are measured without waiting.

scriptedResponses.description: Answer one request with a response derived from recorded bytes: a malformed success, the denial-shaped 404, or a moved resolved version.

quiesce.description: Wait until the client has finished any background work a response started, such as rebuilding connection state.

cancellation.description: Cancel one caller's call through the port's public cancellation surface.
cancellation.notApplicable: The port's public operations take no cancellation signal, token or context.

explicitNullMember.description: Send a request whose optional member is an explicit null through the public API.
explicitNullMember.notApplicable: The port's request types cannot carry an explicit null: an unset member is always omitted from the body.

schemeResourceOperations.description: Read the scheme resources through per-call public operations.
schemeResourceOperations.notApplicable: The port resolves the scheme resources once at connect into connection state, outside the response cache.

sharedRouteOperations.description: Call two public operations that post the same body to the same route.
sharedRouteOperations.notApplicable: The port exposes one method per wire operation, so no two of its operations share a route and body.

A map built in a different order, or an optional member passed as unset, sends the same body and finds the same entry.
An explicit null is a different request from an absent member and gets its own entry.
access.check and context.checkAccess post the same body to the same route and keep separate entries.
A refused request is evicted as it settles, so the next identical call goes back to the server.
A 200 missing a member the contract requires is a failed call: it is not filed, and the next call retries.
Under the opt-in, a decision missing a required member is a failed call and is never filed.
Canceling one of three joined callers settles only that caller; the shared request and its entry survive.
A caller that arrives canceled never touches the cache, and a cancellation after the answer arrived evicts nothing.
The shared request is canceled when its last caller walks away, and not before.
A pinned entry is still served after thirty days, past every per-operation TTL.
An unpinned entry is gone once the one-hour ceiling has passed.
A binding whose version the context token supplies is unpinned too, and its entries expire the same way.
Without the opt-in, every access decision is a wire trip, even on a pinned binding.
With the opt-in on a pinned binding, a repeated decision is answered from its entry.
The opt-in on a binding whose composition can move is refused when the client is built.
The opt-in is refused when the context token, not the client, picks the version.
The never operations reach the wire on every call with the access-decision opt-in off.
The never operations reach the wire on every call with the access-decision opt-in on.
A translation reaches the wire on every call, completed or forbidden, with the access-decision opt-in off.
A translation reaches the wire on every call, completed or forbidden, with the access-decision opt-in on.
A response naming a new resolved version on an unpinned binding clears what was filed under the old one.
The runtime's denial-shaped 404 clears every held entry; the denied call fails and is not replayed.
A 404 that names a missing resource is an answer about that resource and leaves the cache in place.
Mutating one caller's result changes neither a joined caller's result nor a later cached read.
